target_customer: Households in Mexico City who subscribe to weekly boxes of imperfect or surplus produce
problem: Large amounts of edible produce in Latin America are discarded for appearance, size or surplus, while consumers want cheaper groceries.
business_model: Consumer subscription box of surplus produce, sourced directly from producers

founders.name: Jan Heinvirta
prior_employers: Swiss FinTech (founding team member and Head of LATAM)

founders.name: Anahí Sosa
prior_employers: Uber (about five years, led Uber Grocery)

founders.name: Juan Andrade
prior_employers: Walmart (led eCommerce logistics and operations in Mexico)
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by Forbes Mexico; YC page gives first name only.

exit.reason: Forbes Mexico and Descubre.vc report closure for lack of financing; the company declined to comment.

technical_complexity.rationale: Subscription ordering software; the hard part was physical logistics and cold chain, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Sourcing from producers and delivering boxes could be copied by any grocer or delivery app.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established; no dated evidence incumbents sold imperfect produce.

market_need_then: Forbes Mexico reported that 54 percent of fruit and vegetables in Latin America are discarded for appearance, size or surplus, per the Emprendedor piece cited; consumers also wanted savings.

branding.domain_note: Used perfekto.mx, a Mexico country domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positive rescue of food and circular economy message with returnable boxes

branding.brand_signature: Returnable minimal packaging and food rescue counter on the site
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Forbes Mexico, TechCrunch, Springwise, El Universal, TV Azteca and Milenio.

brand_strength.rationale: Broad Mexican and international press and a clear mission, but no evidence of a community or growth driven by the name.

outcome_analysis: Perfekto launched in January 2021, raised 1.1 million dollars pre-seed in November 2022 and reported about 14 million pesos in 2022 revenue, but as a physical business it needed more working capital. It closed on 24 May 2023 after failing to secure more financing per Forbes Mexico and Descubre.vc, so the failure combined a missed next round and heavy capital needs. The unit economics factor reflects the Forbes remark on working capital, not a stated margin.
notes: PitchBook totals 1.34M raised versus 1.1M in the pre-seed, leaving an unlocated gap of about 240K (possibly the YC deal). Education was not found for any founder. Imperfect Foods and Misfits Market are mentioned as models in 2022 coverage, too late to list as competitors as of 2021. The unit_economics tag is a weak inference from working capital needs.
